'''Zamtel''', whose official name is '''Zambia Telecommunications Company Limited''', is a government-owned [[telecommunication]] service provider in [[Zambia]]. Zamtel is one of three mobile phone networks in the country; the others are [[Bharti Airtel|Airtel]] and [[MTN Group|MTN]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.techtrends.co.zm/data-bundle-comparisons-airtel-mtn-zamtel/ |title=Data Bundle Comparisons of Airtel, MTN and Zamtel |date=14 January 2014 |author=TechTrends Staff |publisher=Techtrends.co.zm |location=Lusaka |access-date=9 September 2016}}</ref>

== Company overview ==
Zambia Telecommunications Company Limited is a Company incorporated in Zambia under the Companies Act Chapter 388 of the Laws of Zambia. The sole shareholder of the Company is the Government of the Republic of Zambia. The Company falls under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Transport, Works, Supply and Communications pursuant to [[Gazette|Gazette Notice]] No. 183 of 2012 and the Statutory Functions Act Chapter 4 of the Laws of Zambia.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=zamtel|url=https://www.zamtel.zm/about_company.html|date=2020-05-28|website=zamtel|access-date=2020-05-28}}</ref>

==History==
The first telephone exchange was installed in [[Livingstone, Zambia|Livingstone]], as part of the General Post Office (GPO).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ebizguides.com/ebizpartners_see.php?id_country_sponsors=15&ebizpartnersid=372 |title=The History of Zambia Telecommunications Company Limited (ZAMTEL) |access-date=9 September 2016 |date=2006 |publisher=Ebizguides.com |author=Ebizguides.com |archive-date=18 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160918154249/http://www.ebizguides.com/ebizpartners_see.php?id_country_sponsors=15&ebizpartnersid=372 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1975, the GPO transformed into the Zambian Post and Telecommunication Corporation (PTC).<ref name="Hist">{{cite web |url=http://www.zamtel.zm/about.html |title=The History of Zamtel |access-date=9 September 2016 |date=9 September 2016 |author=Zamtel |publisher=Zamtel |location=Lusaka |archive-date=24 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924214154/http://www.zamtel.zm/about.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In July 1994 the government of [[Zambia]] passed a Telecommunications Act that led to the splitting up of the Post and Telecommunications Corporation into two separate [[companies]]: the Zambia Postal Services Corporation ([[ZamPost|Zampost]]), and the Zambia Telecommunications Company (Zamtel). The Company falls under the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Transport, Works, Supply and Communications of Zambia.<ref name="Hist"/>

In 2010, the Zambian government, under the [[Movement for Multi-Party Democracy]] (MMD) President, [[Rupiah Banda]], sold 75% of the Zamtel to the Libyan company LAP Green Networks. The government claimed it had done so in order to keep Zamtel from shutting down after plans to recapitalize it had failed. This was a contentious move however, as some critics claimed the company was still economically viable.<ref name="Rev">{{cite web| url=http://www.pcadvisor.co.uk/news/network-wifi/zambian-government-reverses-sale-of-zamtel-libyas-lap-green-3329827/ |title=Zambian government reverses sale of Zamtel to Libya's Lap Green |first=Michael | last=Malakata |date=12 January 2012|publisher=Pcadvisor.co.uk |location=London |access-date=9 September 2016}}</ref> The [[Zambian general election, 2011|2011 Zambian national election]] saw the incumbent MMD party replaced by the opposition [[Patriotic Front (Zambia)|Patriotic Front]] (PF). The newly elected government, under President [[Michael Sata]], set out an inquiry into the sale of Zamtel because they believed it was sold fraudulently by the previous government. The inquiry produced a report that showed irregularities in the manner in which Zamtel was sold, alleging that LAP Green and RP Capitals, which was appointed as financial advisor, bribed senior Zambian government officials; an allegation that both LAP Green and RP Capitals denied.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pcworld.com/article/2855612/zambia-pays-loan-for-libyas-lap-green-but-zamtel-case-continues.html |title=Zambia pays loan for Libya's Lap Green, but Zamtel case continues| last=Malakata | date=4 December 2014 |first=Michael |access-date=9 September 2016 | publisher=Pcworld.com |location=San Francisco, California, USA}}</ref> As a result of the findings, President [[Michael Sata]] ordered a reversal of the $257 million deal and the government of Zambia seized control of Zamtel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-16709079 |date=24 January 2012| title=Zambia: President Sata reverses Libyan Zamtel sale |access-date=9 September 2016 |publisher=[[BBC News]]}}</ref>

In 2013, LAP Green sued the government of Zambia in a British court in order to reclaim ownership of Zamtel. The Zambian government agreed that it would compensate LAP Green for its investments, but it would not let ownership of the company be transferred back to the Libyan operator.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.balancingact-africa.com/news/telecoms_en/27546/uk-to-host-lap-green-networks-zambia-lawsuit | title=Zambia: UK to host Lap Green Networks' Zambia lawsuit | access-date=9 September 2016 | last=BAAC News | location=London | publisher=Balancingact-Africa.com (BAAC): Issue Number 649 | date=5 April 2013 | archive-date=14 September 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160914163746/http://www.balancingact-africa.com/news/telecoms_en/27546/uk-to-host-lap-green-networks-zambia-lawsuit | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=30 July 2015 |title=Zamtel, Lap Green Networks saga deepens |url=http://lusakavoice.com/2015/07/30/zamtel-lap-green-networks-saga-deepens/ |access-date=9 September 2016 |publisher=Lusaka Voice |location=Lusaka |archive-date=17 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917083213/http://lusakavoice.com/2015/07/30/zamtel-lap-green-networks-saga-deepens/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Location==
The head office of the company is located in Zamtel House, at the corner of Chilubi Road and Church Road, in the Zambian capital city of [[Lusaka]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zamtel.zm/contact.html | title= Zamtel: Get In Touch With Our Company |date=9 September 2016 |access-date=9 September 2016 | publisher=Zambia Telecommunications Company Limited (Zamtel)| author=Zamtel| location=Lusaka}}</ref> The coordinates of Zamtel House are {{coord|15|24|57|S|28|17|44|E|type:landmark_region:ZM|display=inline}}.<ref>{{google maps| url=https://www.google.com/maps/place/15%C2%B024'57.0%22S+28%C2%B017'44.0%22E/@-15.4158228,28.2933667,434m/data=!3m2!1e3!4b1!4m5!3m4!1s0x0:0x0!8m2!3d-15.415828!4d28.29555 |title=Location of the Headquarters of Zambia Telecommunications Company Limited (Zamtel) |access-date=9 September 2016}}</ref>

==Services==
Services offered by the company include the following:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.zamtel.zm/ |title=Services Offered by Zamtel |last=Zamtel |access-date=9 September 2016 |date=9 September 2016 |location=Lusaka | publisher=Zambia Telecommunications Company Limited (Zamtel)}}</ref>

* '''Zamtel Land-line Services''': Zamtel is the sole fixed-line service provider with approximately 80,000 lines country-wide
* '''Zamtel Prepaid''': Prepaid mobile phone service that allows users to top-up minutes using scratch cards
* '''Zamtel Mobile Internet''': Internet access for mobile devices or computers. 
* '''Zamtel International Roaming service''': International roaming service that allows users to stay connected wherever they are in the world.

===Zamtel Velocity===
In October 2019 Zamtel launched a new unlimited data bundle packages.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sandi |title=Zamtel launches new unlimited WiFi bundles |url=https://www.techtrends.co.zm/zamtel-launches-new-unlimited-wifi-bundles/ |access-date=27 November 2020}}</ref>  The service is available on [[Router (computing)|Router]]s and [[MiFi]]s.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zamtel Velocity Unlimited Internet launched |url=https://www.lensesview.com/velocity-unlimited-internet-launched/#:~:text=Zambia%27s%20first%20unlimited%20wireless%20broadband,market%20and%20uses%20LTE%20technology. |access-date=27 November 2020 |agency=www.lensesview.com}}</ref>

==Corporate governance==
The Industrial Development Corporation in August 2017 appointed a new board of directors for Zamtel. <ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.zamtel.zm/management.html| title=Zamtel Management: Meet The Team |access-date=9 September 2016| publisher=Zambia Telecommunications Company Limited (Zamtel) | author=Zamtel | location=Lusaka}}</ref>
